current_bottleneck: The prior 510a/392a 8/11 frontier is frame-sensitive: 510a drops to 5/11 when rerun on the same 441-window frame used by 593a. 593a is therefore not a collapse from a robust 8/11 baseline, but it also does not add value. Both models share the same hard failures: long-horizon undercoverage, regime layer2 0/8, about 16% persistent undercoverage, level KS 3/25, bad-window coverage around 23-24%, low aggregate kurtosis, and weak active-cell mean-reversion correlation. The learned latent wrapper is a near-neutral perturbation with extra cointegration/skew failure risk.
last_result_summary: 594a reran 510a final checkpoint on the same 441-window frame as 593a. Same-frame 510a scored 5/11, failing coverage, conditionality, time_series, regime_coverage, distributional_fidelity, and mean_reversion. 593a scored 4/11 on the same frame, adding cointegration failure. Metrics were nearly identical on coverage90 (69.6% vs 69.7%), level KS (3/25 vs 3/25), regime layer2 (0/8 vs 0/8), persistent undercoverage (16.2% vs 16.2%), daily-change KS (25/25 vs 25/25), cross-cell corr/rank (1.070/1.225 vs 1.062/1.229), and mean-reversion active pass/corr (75.0%/0.531 vs 75.0%/0.560). 593a costs skewness and worst-cell cointegration without fixing the shared bottleneck.
next_step_recommendation: Close the learned common-latent wrapper branch as an improvement route. The next principled move should target the common broad-frame failure mechanism directly: conditional distribution calibration over whole future paths, especially per-window coverage floor, regime-cell coverage, level location, and active-cell mean-reversion geometry. Do not claim 8/11 robustness without specifying the 192-window frame.
current_best_note: 510a/392a remain the historical short-frame best learned IV laws at 8/11, but 594a shows 510a is only 5/11 on the broader 441-window frame. 574a remains the best risk-manager joint stress product. 593a is clean but below same-frame 510a at 4/11, so it is not a replacement.
oracle_feasibility_note: 435a reaches 11/11 only as a validation-future oracle upper bound; it is not a deployable or learned conditional scenario generator.
